title: Separate Lambda invocation from task outcome

steps.title: Separate Lambda invocation from task outcome

blocks.text: A supplied Lambda task needs bounded permissions and separate invocation and outcome evidence.
The execution role grants the function access to AWS resources during invocation.

Assign the approved role limited to the supplied task’s actions and resources. Invoke with the supplied payload. Inspect returned result and execution logs: invocation success is not proof of operational success.

steps.title: Separate Lambda invocation from task outcome

blocks.text: The supplied function orders-resource-check uses orders-check-role, limited to the approved resource check. Keep its supplied payload unchanged. In the failure case, invocation succeeds but the task result reports failure and the logs support that failure. Do not label the operation successful from invocation status alone. Compare with the case whose task-success result and execution logs support success; record both with role and payload context.

This verifies the bounded task, not every possible operation. The execution role is not unlimited authority. If the task reports an action absent from the approved role, retain permission and result evidence rather than broadening the role during the test. Always separate ability to invoke from permission scope and task outcome.

public.prompt:
Read the supplied Lambda result and logs. Which outcome statement is supported?
```text
{
  "case_id": "task_failed",
  "function": "orders-resource-check",
  "execution_role": "orders-check-role",
  "approved_task_scope": "Only approved actions/resources for the supplied resource check",
  "supplied_payload": "Supplied resource-check payload, unchanged",
  "invocation_status": "success",
  "task_result": "failure",
  "execution_logs": "Resource check completed: expected operation failed.",
  "permission_context": "Do not broaden approved role."
}
```

options.text: Invocation succeeded, but the operational task failed; retain both the returned failure and execution-log evidence.
The operation succeeded because invocation_status is success.
Ignore the result and logs; invocation status is all the operational evidence needed.

o1.message: Invocation status and operational result are distinct; the returned result and logs support task failure.

o2.message: Successful invocation does not override the returned task failure and supporting logs.

o3.message: Operational success must be assessed using the returned task result and execution logs.

correct.message: Invocation status and operational result are distinct; the returned result and logs support task failure.

incorrect.message: Recheck the supplied evidence; configuration or an accepted request alone is not the required outcome.

hints: Compare the invocation status with the task result and log message.

i1.message: This preserves bounded role/payload context and reports task failure rather than inferring success from invocation.

i2.message: The result and logs support success for the bounded supplied task, with unchanged scope and payload.

i3.message: The conclusion contradicts the returned task failure and execution logs.

i4.message: The role scope extends beyond the approved task actions/resources, even if this invocation reports task success.

i5.message: The failed task and permission evidence are retained without treating invocation as operational success or widening authority.

correct.message: Both successful and failed tasks can be correctly judged when scope stays bounded and the conclusion matches results/logs.

incorrect.message: Do not accept a success claim contradicted by logs/results or permissions beyond the approved task.
